clue.text: Destructive types raid coast furiously, led by monarch

indicators.note: led by places the monarch at the front of what follows

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the abbreviation for a queen

indicators.note: doing something furiously means doing it wildly, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Raiders storm a coastline at a king's command, causing havoc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furiously' rearranges RAID COAST into ADICATORS, which the monarch leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who wipe things out are, by their nature, destroyers: types bent on destruction.

clue.text: Become a member again, as penitent person but no pawn

indicators.note: but no says the following item is left out of the word just given

parts.note: someone who repents of their sins
P is the chess notation for a pawn

explanation.surface: A remorseful convert rejoins a group, minus a pawn, as if in a chess club.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoin an organisation is to go back in, an entry made for the second time.

clue.text: Paint is something that can affect dogs badly

definitions.meaning: a water-based paint bound with glue or size, used on walls

definitions.text: something that can affect dogs badly
definitions.meaning: a viral disease of dogs and other animals

explanation.surface: A warning that some paint may harm pets.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both a kind of distemper wall paint and a serious canine illness; two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Guy with a couple of females after church

indicators.note: after puts the church first, with what follows coming behind it

parts.note: F stands for female, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: A man arrives with two women once the church service ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' here is the verb, to make fun of someone, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to tease or ridicule them, which is what banter or light mockery does.

clue.text: Soldier held up by fire, poor thing

indicators.note: held up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A soldier pinned down by gunfire, the poor thing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'held up' means read upwards; 'by' introduces the words that carry the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalryman or private soldier in an armoured or cavalry unit holds this rank.

clue.text: Understand what could be easier will engage learner

indicators.note: will engage means the rearranged word takes in the learner
what could be says these letters may be rearranged into another word

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Learning would be simpler if a student grasped the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what could be' rearranges EASIER into REAISE; 'will engage' sets L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to understand something is to grasp or become aware of it; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Highest-quality 27 as investment in lottery

parts.note: premium goods are top of the range
27 across is a spy, and the most famous fictional spy is James Bond

explanation.surface: A top-class agent described as a gamble in a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: A Premium Bond is a UK government savings bond whose interest is paid as prizes in a monthly draw.
explanation.definitionFit: These British savings certificates keep their capital safe but pay returns as lottery prizes.

clue.text: Provided the last bit expected to be brought in

indicators.note: brought in says one word is placed within the other

parts.note: the end is the final part
something due is anticipated

explanation.surface: The final portion was supplied, as anticipated.
explanation.definitionFit: To be endued with a quality is to be endowed or furnished with it, so supplied.

clue.text: Ultimately manager riles football team

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: to rile is to anger or annoy

explanation.surface: In the end, the boss irritates the club's players.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangers is a famous Glasgow football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasgow Rangers, along with Queens Park Rangers, is a well-known soccer club.

clue.text: An alto sadly lacking a certain musical quality

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A choir alto who unfortunately sings without proper tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonal music has no key or tonal centre, the quality absent here.

clue.text: Yon revolutionary has ceremony befitting right-wing politician

parts.note: yon is an old word for that, pointing to something at a distance
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary
a rite is a ceremonial act

explanation.surface: A rebel over there holds a ritual fit for a conservative MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'befitting' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Margaret Thatcher's free-market Conservative policies is a right-winger.

clue.text: Policeman and doctor let loose

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer
to untie is to free from bonds

explanation.surface: An officer and a medic free a captive.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mountie is a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.

clue.text: Ray maybe keeps work quiet, being wet

indicators.note: keeps means the fish holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a ray is an example of a fish
OP is short for opus, a work
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Ray perhaps keeps his job quiet out of feebleness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name but is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet in British slang means feeble or effete, which suits a dandified, prissy manner.

clue.text: Working for characters in Sunderland

indicators.note: characters in says the letters sit inside the following word

explanation.surface: Someone employed by something in Sunderland, an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Working for a boss puts you beneath them, serving in the sense of being subordinate.

clue.text: Most worthless fool finally attempts to get in touch

indicators.note: to get in places these letters inside the word for touch

parts.note: a pat is a light touch

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before

parts.note: tries are attempts

explanation.surface: An idiot keeps trying to make contact, utterly worthlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry means trivial or meagre, so the superlative is the least valuable of all.

clue.text: Heather, full of terrible dread, is running

indicators.note: full of puts the jumbled letters inside the plant

parts.note: ling is common heather

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters are badly mixed up

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather is filled with awful fear and runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant; 'is running' refers to tights developing a ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: Running is said of tights or stockings when a strip unravels, forming a run or ladder.

clue.text: Footballer getting sacked had an unfortunate effect

parts.note: a back is a defensive football player
fired means dismissed from a job

explanation.surface: A dismissed player's departure went badly for the club.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan backfires when it rebounds with results opposite to those intended.

clue.text: Design firm wants male model

parts.note: CO is short for company
to model for an artist is to pose

explanation.surface: A design company is looking for a man to model.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose is to create or devise, as one designs a piece of music or a layout.

clue.text: Help to a greater extent

definitions.meaning: a verb, to advance or promote a cause

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means advance or promote; as an adverb it means more, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Stein's original potato dish is a hit

indicators.note: original means the first letter of the word

parts.note: mash is mashed potato

explanation.surface: Chef Rick Stein's innovative potato recipe is a success.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash or smash hit is a big success, as a hit show or record is.

clue.text: A little bit in cup soon dissolving

indicators.note: dissolving breaks the letters down so they can recombine

explanation.surface: A trace of something in a cup will soon disappear, like sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupçon, from French, is a very small amount or a slight trace.

clue.text: King with skill, taking time, missing nothing

parts.note: art is skill or craft

indicators.note: missing says the item for nothing is dropped from the time word

parts.note: an hour is a measure of time
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A skilful monarch takes his time but has no gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Legendary King Arthur of Camelot is the monarch named here.

clue.text: Run meal organised for 2 or 3, say

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Arranging a meal for two or three people.
explanation.walkthrough: '2 or 3' looks like a head count; it is an example of a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Digits such as 2 and 3 are examples of figures that stand for numbers.

clue.text: Most insignificant saint buried under meadow

indicators.note: buried under puts the saint below the meadow in this down entry

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or grassland

explanation.surface: A minor saint lies buried beneath a field.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest or slightest is the most trivial; a superlative synonym.

clue.text: Circle with peer and politician, both inadequate

indicators.note: both inadequate means each word falls short, losing its final letter

parts.note: an equal is a peer
a Tory is a UK Conservative

explanation.surface: A lord and an MP, neither up to the job, move in the same circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both inadequate' cuts the last letter from each word, L from EQUAL and Y from TORY.
explanation.definitionFit: The equator is the great circle of latitude round the middle of the Earth.

clue.text: Little woman closed, having not finished, a book

parts.note: Jo March is one of the sisters in Little Women

indicators.note: having not finished drops the end letter of the word

parts.note: shut means closed

explanation.surface: A small woman shut a book before reaching the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Joshua is a book of the Old Testament, following Deuteronomy.

clue.text: Put a hard coat on metal, front edge being lost with corrosion

indicators.note: front edge being lost removes the opening letter of the metal

parts.note: zinc is a metal
rust is corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: Coating metal to protect it, its leading edge eaten away by rust.
explanation.definitionFit: To encrust or incrust is to cover with a hard crust or layer.

clue.text: Spy dispatched, having collected odd bits of gear etc

indicators.note: having collected means the word for dispatched takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: sent means dispatched

indicators.note: odd bits of says the letters come in a strange order

explanation.surface: A spy sent off having gathered spare kit and other oddments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' rearranges GEAR ETC into CRETAGE, held inside SENT; 'odd' tempts towards alternate letters, but those give too few.
explanation.definitionFit: An undercover operative gathering intelligence is a spy.
